column1: # tools/isa-toolchain.tsv -- the population `probe6` runs, one row per build.
# THIS IS THE OWNER.  `tools/tcpay.py emit` generates the payload's thunks, its
# row table and its per-variant compile rules from this file; nothing else may
# declare a probed build.
# WHAT THIS TABLE ASKS, AND WHY IT IS NEITHER OF THE OTHER TWO
#   `tools/isa-payload.tsv`   one encoding per row.  Does this instruction exist
#                             on this die, and does it compute the right answer?
#   `tools/isa-hazard.tsv`    one hand-written SEQUENCE per row.  What does the
#                             pipeline do when a consumer follows its producer
#                             too closely?
#   this file                 one COMPILER INVOCATION per row.  Given a core
#                             whose load-use hazard is measured OPEN at distance
#                             0, does the code this compiler emits for ordinary
#                             C read the stale value?
# The first two ask about the die.  This one asks about the die AND a toolchain
# at the same time, and that is the whole of `R1f` and of `R2c`'s silicon row.
# `plan/router-rebuild-plan.md:1063-1068` (`R1f`) and `:1140-1141` (`R2c`, the
# row that says all three toolchains must reach silicon).
# THE FRAGMENT IS ONE LINE AND IT WAS CHOSEN BY REFUTATION, NOT BY TASTE.
#   tools/rlxprobe/frag.c:   void rlxf(volatile unsigned *d,
#                                      volatile const unsigned *s) { *d = *s; }
# 量 2026-09-14, at the desk, before power.  The first fragment tried was
# `*p ^ seed`, and gcc filled the load delay slot with `jr ra` in ALL NINE
# configurations -- the hazard was never present to be exposed.  That is
# `PROGRESS.md:122`'s stated risk ("a hazard test the compiler has already
# fixed") arriving as a measurement, and `SPEC.md` `TC-07` had recorded the same
# shape two weeks earlier.  Seven candidates were swept with `tools/hazlint`;
# this is the only one that is (a) split by `-march` in every column and (b) has
# ZERO unresolved successors in every column, so `hazlint` can gate it whole.
# WHY IT CANNOT TRAP, WHICH IS THE HALF THE PLAN ASKS ABOUT.  The fragment
# compiles to `lw` + `sw` and nothing else in every column below.  Neither is a
# MIPS32 addition, so no row here can produce the loud failure `probe4` measured
# for `clz`/`clo`/`mul` (`bench/2026-09-14/C1-P4j.log`, ExcCode 10).  A wrong
# answer here can only be a SILENT one, which is what
# `plan/router-rebuild-plan.md` calls 錯誤,且沒有任何警告或 fault.
# THE PREDICTION IS A COMPOSITION OF TWO MEASUREMENTS AND NEITHER IS NEW
#   desk    `SPEC.md` `TC-15` 量: the exposed-`-march` set (4180 4181 5181
#           mips1) pads the load delay slot and the non-exposed set (5280 5281
#           4281 mips2 mips32) does not.
#   silicon `SPEC.md` `CPU-14` 量 seating 21, `bench/2026-09-14/C1-P5j.log`:
#           `lu_sd_d0` reads OPEN -- a store whose DATA operand is the register a
#           load wrote one instruction earlier stores the register's PRIOR value.
# So a row's device prediction follows from its `pad` column and from nothing
# else, and `pad` is itself checked against the artefact by `tcpay verify`.
# **That is what makes this refutable rather than a rehearsal**: a row whose
# build says `nopad` and whose device answer is `lock` refutes `CPU-14` under
# compiler-generated conditions, and a row whose build says `pad` and whose
# device answer is `open` refutes the harness.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated; no `|` anywhere -- `spec-check` C8 counts cells by pipe)
#   vid      the row id.  `v*` is a compiled variant, `c*` a hand-written
#            control.  Used as the thunk's symbol suffix and printed in the
#            report, so it must be [a-z0-9_]+.
#   tc       toolchain key.  `T4` is the host cross-compiler every payload this
#            project has ever run on this die was built with, and it is in the
#            table as the INSTRUMENT'S OWN CONTROL, not as a fourth column of
#            `R2c`.  `T1`..`T3` are the three rsdk releases `R2c` names.
#            `--` for a hand-written control, which no compiler produces.
#   march    the `-march=` value handed to that driver.  `--` for a control.
#   pad      `pad` if the compiler is predicted to put an instruction between
#            the `lw` and the `sw`, `nopad` if not.  讀 for the compiled rows
#            (`TC-15`), and 量 by `tcpay verify` on every build.
#   expect   the device prediction: `lock` (the store writes the LOADED value)
#            or `open` (it writes the register's prior value).  Derived from
#            `pad` plus `CPU-14`; it is NOT an independent guess.
#   why      one sentence.  What this row is for, and what its refutation means.
# THE TWO CONTROLS ARE NOT OPTIONAL AND THEY RUN IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS
#   c_lock   hand-written `lw ; nop ; sw`.  MUST read `lock`.  If it does not,
#            the thunk is not priming the sentinel, or the scratch words are not
#            what the payload believes, and every `open` below is unattributable.
#   c_open   hand-written `lw ; sw`, which is `isa-hazard.tsv`'s `lu_sd_d0` with
#            this payload's own operands.  MUST read `open`.  If it does not,
#            this die's d0 is not open TODAY and no compiled row can be read as
#            evidence about a compiler -- the table is void, not partly valid.
#   Together they are `plan:1074`'s two halves: the positive control establishes
#   that a correct build reads correctly, the negative that this payload can
#   observe the wrong answer at all.  `tcpay.py`'s `check_controls` enforces
#   both and refuses a verdict without them.
# THE THIRD CONTROL IS NOT IN THIS FILE.  Under qemu every row must read `lock`,
# because qemu interlocks.  A qemu run that reproduces the device's `open` rows
# means the harness is reading something other than the hazard.  `tcpay verdict
# --arm qemu` enforces it and it is the forced anti-control, the same shape as
# `hazpay`'s `C4`.
vid
c_lock
column6: POSITIVE CONTROL. Hand-written lw nop sw with this payload's own operands. A correct build reads the loaded value; if this row does not, nothing below is attributable.

column1: c_open
column6: NEGATIVE CONTROL. Hand-written lw sw. isa-hazard.tsv lu_sd_d0 with these operands. Shows this payload can observe the wrong answer at all; if it reads lock the table is void.

column1: v1
column6: THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN CONTROL. Every payload that has ever executed on this die was built exactly here. A refutation of this row is a refutation of probe4 and probe5 as well.
